first_impression.reaction: Santorini is the one everyone's mum suggests, so I came in half expecting blue domes and 'say I do in paradise'. Instead the opener splits the island into areas and tells me how to choose: 'The right one depends on how many guests you are inviting, the ceremony you want and the view you want behind you as you say your vows.' Then the takeaways tell me straight that 'Most cliff-top ceremony spaces hold between 15 and 60 guests'. That's the bit I needed at 60 to 90 guests. Kept reading.

journey.quote: Most cliff-top ceremony spaces hold between 15 and 60 guests, so a larger guest list points to a full-property buyout, a winery terrace or the open-air space at Grand Ambassador in Akrotiri.
journey.reaction: This is the honest trade-off nobody tells you on Instagram. In one line I know the postcard terrace probably isn't us, and I know the three routes that are. Saves me a weekend.

journey.quote: Greek summers bring frequent heatwaves and a wildfire season from June to September, and Santorini sits in an active seismic zone, so plan shade, timing and a fallback for your date.
journey.reaction: Slightly confronting to see 'seismic zone' in the takeaways, but I'd rather hear it here than from Dad. It reads as calm, not scary, and it comes with something to actually do.

journey.section: Santorini wedding venues at a glance
journey.reaction: Good. It doesn't smell like a paid 'best of'. The capacity column is the one I'll actually use with James.

journey.quote: For a larger guest list, the published options are Grand Ambassador, with outdoor space for up to 250 guests, Venetsanos Winery's Upper Terrace for about 100 seated or 160 standing, and a full buyout of Canaves Epitome for up to 170 guests.
journey.reaction: Here's our shortlist, basically handed to me. Three names, three different kinds of day. This is the paragraph I'd screenshot.

journey.quote: Grace Hotel's venue fee includes exclusive use of the selected event spaces, and the hotel quotes room blocks or a resort buyout.
journey.reaction: Exactly the kind of fine print I care about. Not having strangers wandering through our ceremony in their swimmers is a big deal for us.

journey.section: Choosing an area of the island
journey.quote: Choose a winery when wine and a long dinner matter as much as the cliff edge.
journey.reaction: A clear opinion, and honestly it sounds more like us than an Oia balcony. Less try-hard, more about the guests.

journey.quote: Epitome says the Aegean and the caldera frame the moment you say "I do".
journey.reaction: I get that it's the hotel's own line, but 'the moment you say I do' is brochure talk. I skim straight past it. The capacity bullets underneath are what I actually read.

journey.quote: Grace requires a wedding planner for every wedding, engaged at least three months before the day, and the wedding party has a private lounge from 8am.
journey.reaction: Insider-type detail I'd never have found on my own. Also a quiet nudge that we'll need someone on the ground whichever way we go.

journey.quote: The winery invites you to say "I do" with the caldera as your witness, as the sun sets, and its terraces look over the caldera.
journey.reaction: 'The caldera as your witness' is the kind of line my friends would roll their eyes at. Again, it's the winery's phrase, but it's the second 'I do' moment in the venue entries.

journey.quote: For guests with limited mobility, Le Ciel is the one venue here that publishes step-free access.
journey.reaction: Grandparents question answered, at least for one venue. Mum will want to see this line.

journey.section: Getting to Santorini for your wedding
journey.quote: Older guests should know about the stairs before they book. Ask each venue how many steps lie between the road, the rooms and the ceremony space.
journey.reaction: Right instinct, and it's going on our checklist. But it ends on 'ask', and I still don't know how our grandparents get from the airport to a cliff-top hotel in Oia. I'll hold that question for the call.

journey.quote: At Naxos, mean maximums run from 18.7°C in April to 22.1°C in May, about 27°C in July and August, 25.1°C in September and 21.9°C in October.
journey.reaction: Solid numbers, but I'm left doing the maths myself. Is late May or late September the sweet spot? A one-line steer would let me send this straight to Mum and Dad.

journey.quote: A foreign marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of marriage but may not work as proof of a name change.
journey.reaction: Lawyer brain is happy. That's a real, specific gotcha, and the CNI and apostille steps are laid out plainly. Confidence the legal side can be sorted: tick.

journey.quote: Send every venue on your shortlist the same questions, and ask for the answers in writing.
journey.reaction: Twelve good questions. Also exactly the spreadsheet I don't want to spend 18 months on, which is, I suspect, the point.

journey.section: Shortlist your Santorini venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Hidden costs are my biggest fear, so this line does more for me than any 'end-to-end' claim. Paired with 'one person, start to finish' and AUD quotes, it's the right pitch.

unanswered_questions: Have you planned a real Santorini wedding, with venue and date, that I can look at?
For 60 to 90 guests with half flying from Australia, which two or three of these would you actually put on our shortlist?
How do older guests get from the airport or port to a cliff-top venue in Oia or Imerovigli, and do you arrange that?
Which month would you recommend for a Santorini wedding if we want to avoid peak heat and wildfire season but still have the venues open?
Where exactly are Venetsanos Winery and Le Ciel on the island, relative to where guests would stay?
Is someone accountable to us physically on Santorini on the day?

turn_offs_found.turn_off: Clichés: fairytale, dream day, say I do in paradise
turn_offs_found.quote: The winery invites you to say "I do" with the caldera as your witness, as the sun sets, and its terraces look over the caldera.
turn_offs_found.why: 'Say I do with the caldera as your witness' is very close to the 'say I do in paradise' language I skim past, and it's the sort of line that makes Santorini feel cheesy to our friends. It's the winery's phrase, and the rest of the entry is factual, so it's mild, but the plain fact (terraces looking over the caldera) does the job on its own.

turn_offs_found.turn_off: Clichés: fairytale, dream day, say I do in paradise
turn_offs_found.quote: Epitome says the Aegean and the caldera frame the moment you say "I do".
turn_offs_found.why: Same issue, second time: 'the moment you say I do' is brochure copy. Together with the Santo Wines line it nudges a very clear, factual guide toward the tone I'm trying to avoid. Low severity, easy fix.

would_share_with: James (partner): the at-a-glance table and the 'larger guest list' paragraph naming Grand Ambassador, Venetsanos and the Canaves Epitome buyout
Mum and Dad (contributing): the heat, wildfire and seismic section plus the Le Ciel step-free access line, for the grandparents
James again: the booking checklist and the legal section, so we know what we'd be signing up for

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [shortlist your Santorini venues through Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=santorini-wedding-venues&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: Not pushy at all, and 'the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins' plus one person and AUD quotes speak straight to my fears. The checklist makes the case for handing the chasing to someone else. I'd still read another post or two and want to see a real wedding before I enquire, but this one moves me closer.

top_3_changes: Drop or demote the hotels' 'I do' lines ('with the caldera as your witness' at Santo Wines, 'the moment you say "I do"' at Canaves Epitome) and lead with the plain facts, so the venue entries keep the calm, factual tone of the rest of the guide.

In 'When to marry in Santorini', add one plain sentence turning the Naxos figures and the heat and wildfire advice into a steer on which months to look at, so a couple can forward it to parents without doing the maths.

In the getting-there section, add a sentence on what the cliff-top setting means for older guests going from the airport or port to the venue (stairs, luggage, arrival timing), so it doesn't end only on 'ask each venue'.
